analysis.title: Prime HFs Update - Oct 22nd - Broad based de-grossing driven by long selling
key_insights: Hedge funds have de-grossed global equities in 7 of the past 8 sessions, and the pace is accelerating. The last such streak was April 2026, and none occurred in 2025.
Oct 22 was the 5th largest de-grossing day of 2026 at -1.6 SD. It was driven entirely by long selling, the largest since September 2025.

Risk unwinds hit almost every major region on Oct 22. North America led on long sales, Europe saw long sales exceed short covers, and EM Asia saw long sales exceed short sales. China and Hong Kong were the most net sold in Asia, while Taiwan, Korea and Japan were sold more moderately.
De-grossing was broad across sectors, with 9 of 11 global sectors seeing risk unwinds, led by Info Tech and Industrials.

Info Tech saw long selling alongside short additions, its largest net selling since September 2024. Every industry was net sold, led by Semis & Semi Equipment, which was also the most de-grossed. Fundamental L/S funds did most of it, with multi-strats and quants also selling. Semi allocations have dropped back to levels seen earlier in the year.
Industrials were de-grossed mainly by multi-strats and quants across every industry. Oct 22 was the third largest Industrials de-grossing day of the year.
Global AI basket (GSXGGLAI) names saw the largest net selling since end of July. Net and gross allocations are back at the lows seen after the July moves.
Prime book gross leverage is little changed at 312.3% (96th percentile over 5 years), while net leverage fell to 71.8%. The selling cut net exposure far more than gross exposure.
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.1 pts to 47%, at the 1st percentile of the past 3 years and the 5th percentile of 5 years.

At the Oct 22 US close, more than two-thirds of hedge funds were down on the day as concentrated shorts were squeezed further in the second half of the session. For the first time since COVID, all three broad equity strategies fell more than 1% on the same day.

Global Fundamental L/S managers fell 1.4% (-2.1 SD) on Oct 22, the worst day since July 16. Alpha of -0.5% came from China and Info Tech exposures and the concentrated-short squeeze. The group is down 3.8% MTD and up 8.8% YTD. TMT-focused funds fell 2.7% and are down 9.6% MTD.

Global Systematic L/S managers fell 1.3% (-3.4 SD) on Oct 22, the third-worst day since December 2023. All three of the worst days came in the past two months (Aug 19, Oct 15 and Oct 22). The group is still up 19.0% YTD.

Multi-strat equity portfolios (4.5x leverage) fell 1.9% (-3.2 SD) on Oct 22, driven by Momentum, Info Tech, Concentrated Shorts and Crowded Longs. It was their second-worst day since the April 2025 tariff sell-off, behind only July 28.
At noon on Oct 22, Momentum fell 2.6 SD and Crowded Longs fell 2.8 SD. That was the worst daily sell-off in those factors since the week of Liberation Day in April 2025.

Earlier AI-led sell-off on Oct 15: Momentum fell 3.4 SD and Crowded Longs fell 1.8 SD intraday, while Crowded Shorts squeezed +1.2 SD. At the close, Systematic L/S was down 1.4% (-3.7 SD), the worst day since Aug 19. Fundamental L/S was down 0.5% and Multi-strats down 1.2%.
From COVID through end-2025, all three broad HF strategies never fell more than 80bps on the same day. In 2026 it has happened three times: Feb 4, Jul 28 and Oct 22.
risk_factors: Further long selling and de-grossing in Info Tech, Semis and AI-linked names by Fundamental L/S, multi-strat and quant funds.
Squeezes in concentrated shorts and unwinds of Momentum and Crowded Longs, which have produced repeated outsized daily losses in the past two months.
Gross leverage remains high on a 5-year view (96th percentile), so there is more exposure left to cut.
Pain spread across all three broad equity HF strategies on the same day, which has happened three times in 2026 and never between COVID and end-2025.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds have de-grossed in 7 of the past 8 sessions. Oct 22 was the 5th largest de-grossing day of 2026 (-1.6 SD) and the largest long-selling day since September 2025.
Prime book gross leverage is 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year, 96th percentile 5-year) and net leverage is 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year, 37th percentile 5-year).
Global Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 211.7% (63rd percentile 1-year, 92nd percentile 5-year). Net leverage is 47% (1st percentile 3-year, 5th percentile 5-year).
Concentrated shorts squeezed in the second half of Oct 22 while Momentum and Crowded Longs sold off sharply, which compounded losses for quants and multi-strats.
Semiconductor and Semi Equipment allocations are back to levels seen earlier in the year. Global AI basket net and gross allocations are at the lows seen after the July moves.

TMT-focused funds are down 9.6% MTD (still up 8.0% YTD). Asia-focused funds were down 8.8% MTD at noon Oct 22 (up 14.6% YTD). On Oct 15, Asia-focused funds were still up 17% YTD but 23% below their late-June peak of +40%.
